title: Land the corpus safely
intro: A live glide path. Your goal isn't just a corpus — it's arriving de-risked.
briefing: You're 15 years from the goal, gliding 90% equity toward 40% — too hot an arrival, and ₹10k a month won't build the corpus either. Reach ₹75 lakh with equity at 30% or below when you get there. Two levers matter; the crash button will show you why the second one exists.
debrief: The two goals pull against each other, which is the design: more equity for longer builds the corpus faster but arrives hot; gliding to 30% or below costs some growth, so the SIP has to carry more — ₹10k doesn't get there, roughly doubling it does. That tension is every life-cycle fund's actual job, resolved monthly and invisibly. And the crash button is the argument for the second goal: −30% on a 90%-equity book erases years; the same crash at 25% equity is a bad quarter. Sequence risk is why the glide exists.
